_comment: HELD FOR RULING — the batteries census of 12 September 2026, brief 8.
Entries the sector perimeter does not settle. Each carries the source sentence and
what a rule would have to say. NOTHING HERE CHANGES A RULE and nothing here was
decided by this pass: an entry in this file is classed in the census on the reading
stated below, and the class moves if the ruling goes the other way.
This file is not the batteries docket's open questions A–E. Those are about
candidates and predate the census. These are about the census itself.
ALL FIVE WERE RULED ON 13 SEPTEMBER 2026 and each carries `ruling` and `ruled` below.
The questions are kept rather than deleted: a class that moved needs the reason it moved
to be readable beside the reason it was first filed.
Q6 AND Q7 WERE RAISED ON 1 OCTOBER 2026 AND ARE UNRULED, so the line above about all
five being ruled describes Q1–Q5 only. Both came out of reading the Internet Archive
capture of the Morrow bankruptcy report, filed because energy-storage.news now refuses
a declared reader (PR #87). Q6 is a census correction; Q7 is a defect in check_links.
Neither is acted on here and NEITHER CHANGED ANY GATE: the 21 September moratorium holds

Neither is acted on here and NEITHER CHANGED ANY GATE: the 21 September moratorium holds and the entries are held as written until ruled. Q8 joins them on 1 October, from the same push: build_maps' eight status-vs-later-source warnings on six batteries rows.

questions.source_sentence: A bar labelled 'Others', carrying capacity T&E did not attribute to a named works.
questions.the_question: Does a benchmark's own residual row belong in a gap table at all?
questions.reading_taken: Carried in the table with its own class, and never searched. The gate is that the table sums to the list's row count, and dropping the residual would make the table sum to something the publisher did not print.
questions.what_a_rule_would_need_to_say: Either that a residual row is an entry of the list and gets a class of its own — which is this pass's reading — or that the list's entry count for gate purposes is its NAMED rows only, in which case the 2023 gate becomes 50 and the 2024 gate 49, and the class disappears.
questions.ruling: A BENCHMARK AGGREGATE IS NOT AN ENTRY. The class keeps its own name — `benchmark aggregate` — it is never searched, and the gap report says what the row is: a residual with no names. The gate stays at the list's full row count, 51 and 50, because that is what the publisher printed.

questions.source_sentence: quantumscape.com's newsroom: 'PowerCo confirms results: QuantumScape's solid-state cell passes first endurance test'. Salzgitter appears nowhere on the page.
questions.the_question: When an outside list names a cell TECHNOLOGY LICENSOR at a works this register holds under the OPERATOR's name, is that entry a duplicate of the held row or an entry in its own right that fails the admission test?
questions.reading_taken: Not a duplicate. Identifier match is the only duplicate route and nobody has written T&E's entry onto powerco-salzgitter, so calling it a duplicate would be the name join the register retired. It fails on whose works it is.
questions.what_a_rule_would_need_to_say: Whether 'the same works under a different company's name' is a duplicate route distinct from a name-stem join — and if so, what source is required to establish it.
questions.ruling: A LICENSOR IS A SUPPLIER, NOT A PROJECT — the DRI precedent. The entry is a PERIMETER EXCLUSION with the clause 'licensor, no works of its own'. Where the source names the licence to a works that is a row here, the relationship is recorded as an EDGE in the dependency graph: a new edge type `technology_licence` on sector_map.EDGE_TYPES, firmness as the source states it, speaker recorded. The edge is proposed with VERDICT NULL in sources/batteries_edges_proposed.json and is not on the row.

questions.source_sentence: eas-batteries.com confirms the works and the product and states no capacity. Battery-News.de states 0.5 GWh.
questions.the_question: May the perimeter's 1 GWh scale rule be applied using a capacity figure NOBODY BUT AN OUTSIDE LIST has published?
questions.reading_taken: Recorded as failing on scale WITH THE SOURCE OF THE FIGURE NAMED, rather than as a refusal on a number the company never gave. The distinction matters because 'Admission and capacity are separate questions' says a row with no stated capacity stays admitted with an empty capacity — which would pull this entry the other way if the works otherwise qualified.
questions.what_a_rule_would_need_to_say: Whether the scale rule takes any published figure or only the company's and an official record's — the two origins capacity_basis already distinguishes. A benchmark is neither.
questions.ruling: NO. The scale rule is tested on WHAT THE COMPANY STATES; a figure only a list published is the list's claim. The entry is NAMED NOT ADMITTED with the failed leg 'capacity not company-stated', and Battery-News's 0.5 GWh is recorded as a benchmark claim on the entry rather than used to apply the 1 GWh rule. The entry fails because the company has stated nothing, not because 0.5 is less than 1.

questions.source_sentence: The register's standing refusals carry 'VARTA, Ellwangen / Nördlingen | scale | Small-format cells'. Battery-News carries V4Smart at Nördlingen, which is the VARTA/Porsche venture.
questions.the_question: Does a standing refusal of a company's works at a town cover a DIFFERENT venture's works at the same town?
questions.reading_taken: It does not. The entry was searched on its own — varta-ag.com/en answers 200 and names neither Nördlingen nor V4Smart — and recorded as searched rather than folded into the VARTA refusal. Folding it in would have refused a works on a clause written about a different one.
questions.what_a_rule_would_need_to_say: Whether a refusal is keyed to the company, the works, or the pair — and what happens when a joint venture takes over a refused works.
questions.ruling: A REFUSAL ATTACHES TO A PROJECT AND ITS OWNER, NEVER TO A TOWN. V4Smart is worked as its own entry from its own sources. Seven fetches across v4drive.com, v4smart.de and varta-ag.com: the company is confirmed as making high-power cells and names no site and no capacity anywhere. SEARCHED, NONE FOUND — on its own evidence, not on VARTA's.

questions.source_sentence: One row: 'SK innovation | Komarom & Ivancsa | 2028 | 47.3 GWh'.
questions.the_question: How does a gap table count one benchmark row that covers two works this register holds separately?
questions.reading_taken: One entry, one class, with both row ids on it. The table counts benchmark ROWS, because the gate is that it sums to the list. The 47.3 GWh is not split: nothing here can divide it.
questions.what_a_rule_would_need_to_say: Whether the gap table's population is the list's rows or the works behind them — and, if the latter, how a capacity stated once for two works is handled, given this register does not apportion figures.
questions.ruling: ONE LIST ENTRY, TWO WORKS HERE. The benchmark reference is recorded on BOTH rows, the entry is counted ONCE as held, and the list's 47.3 GWh stays on the list side as its claim — nothing here splits it. The reference debt stands as written.

questions.source_sentence: Morrow gave four reasons for the bankruptcy: competition in the global battery market has intensified and brought prices down / capital costs have increased / there have been delays in its industrialisation process / the investment market has become more restrained
questions.the_question: The row's stop_reason_note says two of Morrow's four reasons are off the file because the fetch did not carry them. The capture carries all four. Does the note get corrected, and does stop_reason grow past ['finance', 'cost']?
the_four_reasons_as_captured: competition in the global battery market has intensified and brought prices down
there have been delays in its industrialisation process
the investment market has become more restrained
questions.the_notes_current_text: 'it was not possible to complete the process of securing a new industrial investor and financing the group in light of constraints imposed by the group's liquidity situation'. The report says the company gave FOUR reasons and quotes one of them, 'capital costs have increased'; that is the second value here, and the other two are not on this file because the fetch did not carry them.
questions.why_the_note_was_right_when_written: The live fetch of 2026-09-11 hit the premium interstitial, which sits between the third paragraph and the reason list. The note is an honest record of what that body carried. The capture of 2026-09-12 carries the list in full, so this is a better copy of the same document rather than a different document — and it is the copy the row now cites.
questions.the_notes_own_arithmetic_does_not_add_up: It says the company gave FOUR reasons, quotes ONE, and calls the remainder the other TWO. Four minus one is three. Whatever the ruling on the reasons, that sentence is wrong as written.
questions.reading_taken: NONE, and deliberately. The row is held exactly as it stands: the note, the verbatim and stop_reason are untouched by PR #87, which swapped the URL and the citation dateline and nothing else. Changing a reason vocabulary mid-pass is what the 21 September moratorium forbids.
questions.what_a_rule_would_need_to_say: Whether stop_reason takes a value per reason the company states — which would add a market or demand value for the first and fourth, and a schedule value for the third, if those exist in the vocabulary — or whether it stays the two-value summary it is and only the note is corrected. The second is the smaller change and leaves the cross-sector counts alone; the first makes the row say what the company said. They are not the same question as fixing the arithmetic, which is wrong either way.

questions.source_sentence: 26 of the 384 live-checked URLs are on web.archive.org, and a sweep that cannot reach the host reports every one of them as 'reported, not failed' and exits 0.
questions.the_question: A sweep that cannot reach web.archive.org passes without checking any archive URL. Should an unreachable host be a silence the gate refuses rather than a soft report?
questions.how_it_was_found: Three check_links sweeps in one afternoon, plus the fetches behind PR #87, got this machine rate-limited by web.archive.org. All 26 archive URLs then returned URLError errno 61, connection refused. status_of raises OSError, the caller files it in `soft`, and the gate printed 'reported, not failed' and exited 0 — including for the one URL that pull request had just added and whose whole purpose was to be checkable. The same 26 answered 200 through the gate's own client once the limit expired, so nothing was wrong with any of them.
questions.why_this_is_the_shape_the_repository_alr: It is D-S1's shape one layer out. There the index recorded a fetch that had happened and returned nothing, and twenty works looked searched. Here the gate records a check that could not happen and 26 citations look checked. check_fetch_records draws exactly this line for fetches — a publisher refusal is an answer, a client-side failure is not — and check_links does not draw it for sweeps.
questions.why_a_soft_report_is_nevertheless_defens: A contributor on a bad connection is still entitled to push, which is why OSError is soft in the first place. A gate that fails on any network hiccup is a gate that gets switched off, and that reasoning is written into this repository in several places.
questions.what_a_rule_would_need_to_say: Where the line sits between a flaky URL and an unreachable HOST. One shape: count the unreachable per host, and fail when every URL on a host is unreachable while other hosts answer — which separates 'the network is down' from 'this one host is refusing us', and would have failed the afternoon described above while still passing on a single timeout. A rate limit is also not a refusal of the resource, which is the distinction the 429 branch already makes by asking twice; errno 61 arguably deserves the same second ask.
questions.not_done_here: check_links is NOT changed by PR #87 and must not be. The gate is being ruled on, not amended, and the branch that found the defect is the wrong branch to fix it in.

questions.source_sentence: build_maps: check the status — acc-kaiserslautern is cancelled as of 2026-02-07, and carries a later source (2026-09-07, Automotive Cells Company: "Kaiserslautern — ACC is actively preparing for its deployment in Germany") that its status has not been read against — the split now decides whether it is drawn
questions.the_question: Eight warnings on six rows: a cancelled or paused row carrying a source dated after the status event, which nothing has read the status against. Is each a status to re-read, or is the warning asking a question the dates cannot answer?
questions.how_it_surfaced: Printed by build_maps on the pre-push chain of PR #87, which touches none of these rows. Reported, not failed, and pre-existing. Recorded here rather than acted on because the branch that saw them is the Morrow 403 branch.

the_eight_warnings_by_row.status_speaker: press (CNBC, carrying ACC's own statement to unions)

later_sources.speaker: Evertiq
later_sources.title: ACC shelves Termoli gigafactory – unions push for mechanical production

later_sources.speaker: Automotive Cells Company
later_sources.title: Kaiserslautern — ACC is actively preparing for its deployment in Germany
later_sources.quoted: Operation should start in 2025 with an initial capacity of 13,4GWh that will ultimately ramp-up to 40 GWh.
later_sources.reads_against_the_status: YES, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE OF THE EIGHT THAT DOES. The owner's own site, in September 2026, still says it is actively preparing a site the owner abandoned in February 2026, and still promises a start in a year already past.
later_sources.but: THE PAGE CARRIES NO DATE, on the page or in its markup, and 2026-09-07 is the RETRIEVAL date — the row says so. So it is later by when somebody fetched it, not by anything the company dated. An undated evergreen page is not a new statement about status; it is an old page nobody took down.

the_eight_warnings_by_row.what_the_row_already_says: The row records the tension in the open, in the stated_schedule note: 'the register reads, in September 2026, a company page still promising a 2025 start for a project the company abandoned in February 2026 — the statement is recorded as found, not corrected.' So this warning is not news to the row. The question is whether the register should go further than recording it.

later_sources.speaker: Landesamt für Vermessung, Geoinformation und Landentwicklung Saarland
later_sources.title: INSPIRE-WFS SL Flurstücke Grundstücke ALKIS
later_sources.reads_against_the_status: no, and it cannot. It is the cadastral WFS capabilities document cited for where the parcels are. A parcel layer says nothing about whether a project is alive, and its 2026-09-05 is the retrieval date.

the_eight_warnings_by_row.note: THIS ROW CARRIES OTHER LATER SOURCES THE WARNING DID NOT NAME — Gemeinde Überherrn on 2026-06-29, and two on 2026-05-08 — all of them the revocation of the site's development plan, which corroborates the cancellation. build_maps appears to warn on the newest source only, which is worth knowing when reading the eight as a set.

later_sources.speaker: NOVO Energy AB
later_sources.title: About us — NOVO Energy
later_sources.reads_against_the_status: not really. It is an 'About us' page cited for capacity — 'a potential annual cell production capacity of up to 50 gigawatt hours' — and it is silent on the pause either way.
later_sources.but: The page carries no date; 2026-09-07 is the retrieval date, as the row says.

later_sources.speaker: The Gazette (The London Gazette)
later_sources.title: POWER BY BRITISHVOLT LIMITED — Appointment of Administrators, notice 4260297
later_sources.reads_against_the_status: no — administrators appointed two days after is the cancellation's own paperwork

later_sources.speaker: Companies House
later_sources.title: Insolvency — POWER BY BRITISHVOLT LIMITED (12381543)
later_sources.reads_against_the_status: no — it carries the ending as well as the beginning: administration 17 January 2023 to 28 October 2024, then a creditors' voluntary liquidation. A dead company is more cancelled, not less.
later_sources.but: 2026-09-06 is the retrieval date of a register view, not a new event.

later_sources.speaker: Battery-News.de
later_sources.title: SVOLT withdraws from Brandenburg battery site
later_sources.reads_against_the_status: no — it is the next day's report of the same withdrawal

later_sources.speaker: Elektronik (WEKA Fachmedien)
later_sources.title: Vorerst keine Batteriezellen-Fabrik in Sachsen-Anhalt
later_sources.reads_against_the_status: no — and its headline is the pause: 'no battery cell factory in Saxony-Anhalt FOR NOW' is the same reading as `paused`.

questions.what_the_eight_actually_are: SEVEN OF THE EIGHT CORROBORATE THE STATUS OR ARE SILENT ON IT, and three of those are undated pages whose recorded date is the day this register fetched them. Only acc-kaiserslautern's own site reads against its row, and that row already says so in writing. So the warning is ordering dates, not comparing statements — which is all a builder can do without reading, and is why it is a report and not a gate.
questions.reading_taken: NONE. No row is touched, by PR #87 or here. Every status stands as recorded.
questions.what_a_rule_would_need_to_say: Three things, and they are separable. FIRST, whether a source whose recorded date is a RETRIEVAL date can be 'later' than a status event at all — on these six rows it is what generates three of the eight, and arguably it should never fire, because the comparison wants two datelines and one of them is a fetch. SECOND, whether the warning should name every later source or only the newest: svolt-uberherrn has four and was warned on one. THIRD, and the only one about the register rather than the builder, what a row should do when an owner's own undated page contradicts a status the owner itself announced — record it as found, as acc-kaiserslautern does, or carry an explicit field saying the owner's site has not caught up. The first two would quiet seven of these eight without reading anything.
